brief_summary: This study will evaluate the efficacy and safety of AZD6234 compared with placebo in adults who are overweight or obese, with or without type 2 diabetes mellitus.
brief_title: A Study to Evaluate the Effectiveness and Safety of the Drug AZD6234 for Managing Weight in Adults Who Are Obese or Overweight. These Participants May or May Not Also Have Type 2 Diabetes

eligibility.criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Aged 18 years or older at the time of signing informed consent.
* Body mass index:
* at least 28 kg/m²; or
* at least 24 kg/m² and less than 28 kg/m² with at least one protocol-defined weight-related comorbidity, including type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypertension, dyslipidaemia, obstructive sleep apnoea, cardiovascular disease, heart failure, chronic kidney disease, metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease, knee osteoarthritis, or stress urinary incontinence.
* Stable body weight (≤ 5% body weight change) for at least 3 months prior to Randomisation.
* Participants with type 2 diabetes mellitus must:
* have been diagnosed at least 6 months before informed consent;
* have HbA1c between 6.0% and 10.0% at Screening; and
* be managed with diet and exercise alone or with a stable dose of 1 to 3 oral glucose-lowering medications for at least 3 months before Screening.
* At least one previous self-reported unsuccessful attempt to lose body weight.
* Participants of childbearing potential must comply with protocol-defined highly effective contraception requirements and have negative pregnancy tests at Screening and Randomisation.
* Able to provide signed informed consent.

Exclusion Criteria:

* Obesity primarily caused by another endocrine disorder.
* Severe heart failure, defined as New York Heart Association Class IV, or hospitalisation for heart failure within 3 months before Screening.
* Type 1 diabetes mellitus or ketoacidosis or hyperosmolar coma/state within 3 months before Screening.
* Clinically significant gastric-emptying abnormality requiring treatment.
* Significant inflammatory bowel disease or another severe disease or prior surgery affecting the upper gastrointestinal tract.
* Cardiovascular event, percutaneous coronary intervention, or coronary artery bypass graft within 3 months before Screening.
* Previous or planned surgical treatment for obesity.
* Uncontrolled hypothyroidism or hyperthyroidism.
* Significant hepatobiliary disease, including protocol-defined elevations in alanine aminotransferase, aspartate aminotransferase, or total bilirubin.
* Neoplastic disease within 5 years before Screening, except as otherwise permitted by the protocol.
* Clinically important disease or disorder that may place the participant at risk or interfere with study participation.
* Known or suspected drug abuse or alcohol abuse.
* Planned elective surgery requiring discontinuation of study intervention for more than 6 weeks.
* Weight-management treatment within 3 months before Randomisation.
* Treatment with a glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist or another glucagon-like peptide-1-containing medication within 3 months before Randomisation.
* Treatment with a marketed or investigational amylin-based compound within 3 months before Randomisation.
* Use of insulin therapy for type 2 diabetes mellitus.
* Long-term systemic glucocorticoid treatment lasting more than 14 days or use of central nervous system stimulants.
* Concomitant medication that may increase risk, affect study results, or interfere with study participation.
* Unstable major depressive disorder or Patient Health Questionnaire-9 score of 15 or higher.
* History of psychosis or active symptomatic bipolar disorder.
* Active suicidal ideation corresponding to Category 4 or 5 on the Columbia-Suicide Severity Rating Scale, or history of a suicide attempt.
* Participation in another clinical study within 30 days before Screening.
* Known hypersensitivity to AZD6234.
* Involvement in the planning and/or conduct of the study.
* Unlikely or unable to comply with study procedures, restrictions, or requirements.
* Previous randomisation in the present study.
* Currently pregnant or breastfeeding.
* Any other condition that, in the Investigator's judgement, makes participation inappropriate.

official_title: A Phase III, Randomised, Double-Blind, Placebo-Controlled, Multicentre Trial to Evaluate the Efficacy and Safety of AZD6234 in Participants With Obesity or Overweight With at Least One Weight Related Comorbidity With or Without Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus (SELENE-Asia)

primary_outcomes.measure: Percent change in body weight from baseline at Week 64
Number of participants achieving at Least a 5% Reduction in Body Weight From Baseline at Week 64
